findings.title: Line I (the first open line) needs a developer.paypal.com sandbox account and native key dialogs; nothing in the app helps him get them
findings.expected: A newcomer with an ordinary PayPal business account is told in one sentence what the keys are and how to get them, or the first line is something he can finish (rules).
findings.got: Charter opens on Line I 'Add your PayPal sandbox keys' (firstOpenLine = first undone). The only guidance is a sub-line 'registering at developer.paypal.com creates a sandbox business account with its test keys' and an (i) popover. No link, no steps, no 'this is not your real PayPal login'. The keys are typed into Windows dialogs, one per key. 'Sandbox' and 'keys' are words Omar does not own.
findings.code_check: confirmed-absent (no link or how-to anywhere: grep developer.paypal under src returns only the two strings above)
findings.l2_priority: Observe what a person with only a normal PayPal business login does at Line I. Precondition: native Windows shell with real credentials dialog (preview mock cannot show the OS dialogs); mark uncertain on a browser host.
findings.suggested_acceptance: From Line I a person with no developer account can reach a plain 3-step explanation (what, where, how long) without leaving the window blind; or Line I is not first when no keys exist and a rules-first order is offered.

findings.title: Practice deal step cannot complete in a plain build, and the Charter then stays the Home screen with no skip in real mode
findings.expected: If the house seller is unreachable the step says so once, can be set aside, and the wallet's normal home shows; the owner is never parked on setup.
findings.got: In a build without the house pin or relay the practice line shows 'not set up in this copy' (twice) and offers nothing. gettingStarted().show stays true while any step is undone and no other wallet is connected, so the Home layer remains the Charter (CentreLayer renders Charter when firstRun). Skip exists only when backend().kind === 'mock' (preview). The 'Done' button appears only when all lines are done. Tabs still open modules, so he is not locked out, but 'Your first safe deal in 4 steps' can never finish. The HOUSE-not-deployed fact itself is an ACCEPTED gap and is not counted here; the consequence (permanent Charter, no honest skip) is not accepted.
findings.code_check: present-broken (logic traced: show = firstRun===true || (firstRun===false && done<total && otherConnections===0); practice done only when counterparty_list has house)
findings.l2_priority: Precondition: native shell or mock world with house = 'unavailable' (mock default first_run world has house 'idle', so it must be forced; if it cannot be, resolve uncertain and say a fixture with settings.house=unavailable is needed). Then sign a rule and check what Home shows.
findings.suggested_acceptance: With house unavailable: practice line reads as one calm sentence, is marked 'later', and Home shows the decision centre once rules are signed.

findings.title: Getting the app running needs a terminal, a Rust toolchain and (for the relay) an environment variable
findings.expected: Install is a double click; nothing before the Charter needs a terminal.
findings.got: No installer (bundle inactive). README: rustup, pnpm install, pnpm build, cargo run -p table-desktop; relay is set with $env:TABLE_RELAY_URL in PowerShell and cannot be set in the app. This is before Omar ever sees the tour. Outside the designed in-app surface, so it caps the journey's reachable audience to developers.
findings.code_check: confirmed-absent (README states 'There is no signed installer')
findings.l2_priority: None for L2 on a browser host (not drivable). Needs a product decision, not a browser run.
findings.suggested_acceptance: A signed installer exists, or the journey is formally scoped to technical owners and Omar's segment is declared out of scope.

findings.title: First rule cannot be signed until he types a 'payee name' (a no-spaces code) he does not have yet; the prefill is empty on a new wallet
findings.expected: Ready-made rules and Say it produce a signable draft; anything the wallet cannot know is asked in his words.
findings.got: Every template and every Say-it draft includes a payees clause. Prefill comes from already-connected wallets (connectedPayees), but connecting comes after rules (Line III). On a new wallet it is empty; validation then blocks signing: 'list at least one payee', and a name with spaces is refused ('use letters, digits and - _ . : @ + only, no spaces'). The field label 'Who may they pay?' with placeholder 'packrite-supply, cablehaus' and hint 'payee names of the shops you use'. The haggler template also needs an 'item code' ('monitor-24-ips') 'as the seller lists it'. Say it shows 'May pay: you choose' and defers the problem to the approval window.
findings.code_check: present-broken for a no-connections wallet (empty payees fails build() validation)
findings.l2_priority: Precondition: first_run=1 mock world (nobody connected). Pick 'Careful', leave payees blank, try Review & sign; record exactly what Omar sees. Also try 'Leather Supply Co' as the payee.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Signing a first rule needs no identifier he must invent: either 'any shop I connect later' is a first-class choice, or the field accepts a shop name and the wallet derives the code.

findings.title: No agent app installed: the agent step shows an empty list and no sentence; with one installed it is still always 'not connected' with engineer reasons
findings.expected: 'No agent app found on this computer. That is fine: the practice agent plays your deals.' Reasons in plain words.
findings.got: No CLI on the PATH means the runtime never attaches it, engine_status returns only the practice agent, and the picker filters that one out, leaving an empty radio group and no empty-state text (the only text shown is for loading or error). The gold 'Keep the practice agent for now' button is there, so the step is finishable (good). When a CLI is installed, the probe always reports it unavailable, and the reason shown is passed through unchanged: 'The wallet can't yet confirm this agent app reaches only the wallet's own tools', or 'Engine version probe failed' when the probe errors. Neither tells Omar what to do. The step is titled 'Choose your agent app' although no choice exists today.
findings.code_check: present-broken (empty state missing; reason strings are engineering text, reasonWords has no entry for them)
findings.l2_priority: Precondition: native shell on a host with neither CLI installed (this host: unknown; mock fixtures always list both, so the empty list cannot be reproduced in the preview). Resolve uncertain on a browser host and name the fixture: engines = [scripted] only.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Agent step with zero agent apps shows one plain sentence and the gold keep-practice button; reason strings pass through reasonWords with plain replacements.

findings.title: Machinery and product names reach user-facing strings, against the project's own rule
findings.expected: UX-GUIDE principle 3 and the vocabulary table: no vendor/engine names, no 'owner key', no 'payee', no 'item code'.
findings.got: Strings Omar sees: 'claude-code' and 'codex-cli' (tour stop main.engine, tumbler.engine, approval.engine; Charter radio label {e.id}; Settings row; START_STEP.engine.sub); 'owner key' ('Sign with your owner key', 'Signed with: your owner key, after Windows Hello'); 'Idle-locked' and 'owner configuration' (inline toasts/tooltips in Handoff); 'sandbox' / 'Sandbox' mode badge (explained only in a hover tooltip); 'payee'; 'item code'; 'four words'; 'charter', 'Line II of V'. UX-GUIDE itself contradicts: 'Never vendor names (AGENTS.md)' vs 'keep the product id as the value'. words/setup.ts is an empty stub (export {} only) while its header says every setup string lives there, and the setup strings are inline in words.ts and Handoff, so the audit surface the guide promises does not exist.
findings.code_check: confirmed (strings read verbatim; counted below in the report)
findings.l2_priority: Visual confirmation of which strings are visible without hover; precondition none (preview ok).
findings.suggested_acceptance: Zero hits for the banned list in rendered first-run surfaces; setup strings live in words/setup.ts or the stub is removed and the guide corrected.

findings.title: Three separate tours (main 5 stops, tumbler 4, approval 4), each skipped separately; the approval tour fires at the first signature
findings.expected: One skip silences the tour everywhere, and nothing coaches over the moment of signing.
findings.got: Progress is stored per window. Skipping the main tour does not skip the approval window's tour (OwnerConfig mounts Tour with firstRun={first}); the tumbler tour starts whenever the start facts exist (firstRun={!!start}). Skip works (Esc or Skip tour), persists in localStorage with in-memory fallback, and 'Take the tour' reopens: resume is sound. Counted cost: up to 13 coach marks plus 3 skip actions.
findings.l2_priority: Check whether the approval tour covers the Sign button or Hello prompt. Precondition: first_run=1 world.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Skipping once suppresses the new-tour auto-start in the other windows.

findings.title: What-if shows counts, not dollars, and on a brand-new wallet it has nothing to show; the sign sheet then says 'No deal this week would have gone differently'
findings.expected: Journey definition of done: the rule's effect on last week is shown in dollars before signing.
findings.got: summaryWords returns 'would have refused N, asked you about N, allowed N' or, for an empty week, 'No deals this week to try these rules on.' No dollar figure anywhere in simulation.ts/WhatIf summary. SignSheet appends ' No deal this week would have gone differently.' whenever hits is empty, which for an empty week is vacuous reassurance. First rule on a first-run wallet always has an empty week (no deals), so Omar's first signature carries zero what-if value. hitPhrase also puts deal labels ('D-0190 (title)') into the sentence.
findings.code_check: confirmed-absent for dollars (formatMoney is imported in WhatIf.tsx but summaries and sentences carry counts only; verify per-row amounts at L2); vacuous sentence confirmed
findings.l2_priority: WhatIf.tsx rows may show amounts per deal: confirm on a world that has deals. Empty-week sentence: first_run=1 world.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Empty week says 'Nothing to compare yet: your first week starts now'; non-empty week states the amount the rule would have stopped or let through.

findings.title: Windows Hello is a hard requirement for line I, II and V; when it is not set up the lock card ends in 'Not supported' with no way forward
findings.expected: A newcomer without Hello is told how to turn it on or offered an alternative way to confirm it is him.
findings.got: Handoff toast says 'unlock with Windows Hello there first'. If native_reauth_available is false the lock card shows 'Not supported: Windows Hello isn't set up on this computer, so this window can't unlock. Nothing was unlocked.' and no button. Sign, save keys, connect are all behind it. Dead end for a Home-edition machine without a PIN or biometric.
findings.code_check: present-broken for the unsupported branch (no instructions, no fallback)
findings.l2_priority: Precondition: settings.native_reauth_available=false (mock fixture sets true; needs a fixture flip or a real host without Hello). Uncertain on this host until built.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Unsupported branch says how to set up Windows Hello (one sentence and where) and the Charter marks the lines blocked by it.

findings.title: Counts disagree and 'signed' is used for things that are not signatures
findings.got: Title says 'Your first safe deal in 4 steps' (START_ORDER) while the Charter shows five lines (I to V, adds Unlock) and '{n} of 5 lines signed'; connecting a house seller and choosing an agent app are tagged 'signed'. The tumbler and approval window show four steps. Line II screen carries two competing actions: 'Sign rules ↗' (default) and Say it's 'Review rules' (gold), plus 4 try-lines, mic, Read it, Clear.
findings.l2_priority: Count visible controls on the Line II screen at 1x. Precondition: first_run=1.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Same number of steps on every surface; 'done' not 'signed' for non-signatures; one gold action per Charter line.

findings.title: Practice vs real is carried by the word 'Sandbox' and a hover tooltip; 'practice' appears in the app only for the agent and the house shop
findings.expected: A permanent plain-language label that no money is real, visible without hover.
findings.got: Mode badge text is 'Sandbox' (title: 'PayPal's test money. Nothing here is real money.'). In a browser preview a second badge 'Preview · sample data' shows. The safety promise ('Nothing pays without you or a rule you signed. Waiting never sends money.') is visible on the Charter and strong. But Omar's first thought on 'Sandbox' is a place for children; the test-money meaning lives in the hover. Nothing in this build can move real money (README), so the real risk is the opposite: he may believe a real PayPal account is connected after Line I.
findings.l2_priority: Check badge visibility in main footer and approval header at first launch. Precondition: none.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Badge reads 'Test money' (or sandbox plus a visible half-line) on every window; Line I done-state says 'Connected to PayPal's test side'.

findings.title: Skip and resume are real: step state derives from the wallet's facts, the tour persists, and the safety promise is on the first screen
findings.got: Charter lines are all clickable (any order, onStep), 'done' derives from settings, mandate_list and counterparty_list so a restart resumes at the first open line; tour skipped/finished is stored and 'Take the tour' reopens; handoff windows that close unfinished say 'Not finished yet. Nothing has changed.' and offer Reopen. The 'If you do nothing' / 'no money moves' lines are on every handoff.
findings.l2_priority: Reload mid-flow and confirm the same line shows. Precondition: first_run=1 world (own storage key).

findings.title: Say it reads one sentence into plain chips, labels what it filled in safely, never signs, and the sign sheet states consequences in plain words with 'If you close this: nothing is signed'
findings.expected: He can say a rule in his words and see what it means before the gate.
findings.got: Fixed word list (no AI, said so), 'You said / I filled in (change any) / Not sure' chips, one question at a time, example sentences, 'Review rules' hands a typed draft to the approval window. Sign sheet: diff table, 'In plain words', 'Applies to: every new request', closing line with silence consequence. Wallet limits sit 'one cap above every rule' (RULES_CARD, RULES_EXPLAIN) in the Rules area.
findings.code_check: present-and-working (wallet-wide limits above agent rules is stated in words; whether it is visible during signing is not shown in the sign sheet, verify at L2)
findings.l2_priority: Say a sentence from first_run=1 and compare read-back with the editor. Precondition: none.

findings.title: Missing engine does not block: the agent step has a gold 'Keep the practice agent for now' that counts as done, and nothing before it waits on an engine
findings.got: engineChosen('scripted', ..., chosen) is done only after the explicit keep; START_ORDER puts the agent step last 'because nothing before it waits on it'.
